sections.heading: Why a hierarchy
points: Fast memory is expensive per byte, so there is little of it.
Registers -> L1 -> L2 -> L3 -> RAM -> disk: each level is bigger and slower.
It works only because programs show locality.

sections.heading: The two localities
points: Temporal: what was used recently will be used again (loops, counters).
Spatial: what is near what was used will be used (arrays, code).

sections.heading: Numbers to be able to compute
points: Average access = hit time + miss rate x miss penalty.
At 95% hits, 1 ns hit and 100 ns penalty, the average is 6 ns, not 1.
Misses are classified as compulsory, capacity or conflict.

sections.heading: Splitting an address
points: offset = log2(block size), index = log2(number of sets), tag = everything left.
Direct-mapped: one line per set. Fully associative: one set, no index bits.
Three kinds of miss: compulsory (first touch), capacity (cache too small), conflict (wrong mapping).

sections.heading: Traps the quiz likes
points: Longer cache lines stop helping and start hurting.
Direct-mapped gives each block exactly one possible line.
Write-back needs a dirty bit; write-through does not.
